perf.summary: Build3D/Query3D silently ignore the z coordinate and bounds, returning 2D results — a correctness/semantics trap rather than a perf win.
perf.currentCost: Build3D (line 101) forwards to Build2D dropping zs entirely; Query3D (line 107) drops z1/z2. Any caller treating this as a real 3D interval/segment structure gets wrong results — and the unused z parameters mislead the API.
perf.proposedChange: Either implement true 3D (carry z interval into Node and test z overlap in Query) or rename/remove the 3D entry points so the API does not advertise unsupported behavior. If 3D is intentionally out of scope, drop the methods to avoid dead-parameter confusion.
perf.rationale: Purity/ergonomics: the function is not doing what its name promises; fixing or removing it prevents silent wrong answers and clarifies the API contract.
perf.risk: This is a semantics correction, not a behavior-preserving micro-opt — flag for owner decision. If callers currently rely on the 2D-forwarding behavior, removing it is breaking.

perf.summary: Child Min/Max merge re-loads nodes[Left]/nodes[Right] up to four times each through repeated indexing.
perf.currentCost: Lines 62-71 access nodes[rootIdx].Left and nodes[nodes[rootIdx].Left].Min/.Max via chained indexing multiple times (e.g. nodes[nodes[rootIdx].Left].Min appears in both the compare and the assign). Each is a dependent pointer-add + load; the compiler may not prove no-alias to fold them.
perf.proposedChange: Cache `int lft = nodes[rootIdx].Left;` then `Node* lc = &nodes[lft];` and read `lc->Min`/`lc->Max` once into locals before the compares. Same for Right. Also hoist `nodes[rootIdx]` into `Node* self = &nodes[rootIdx];`.
perf.rationale: Collapses repeated address computations and loads into single local reads, shortening the dependency chain of the bottom-up merge done at every internal node.
perf.risk: Pointers are stable for the duration (no reallocation), so caching addresses is safe. Semantics identical.

perf.summary: Inner partition loop reloads xs[idx[i]]/xs[idx[j]] with double indirection per comparison; same hoist as RangeTree applies.
perf.currentCost: Lines 35,39,41 do nested gather xs[idx[*]] each comparison. The double indirection (idx then xs) per compare is a long dependency chain repeated O(n) per level.
perf.proposedChange: Within this single-axis build, the values being partitioned are always xs[idx[*]]; this is already minimal, but the pivot `xs[idx[k]]` is reloaded as the loop may move idx[k]. Hoisting pivot into a local `double pivot` (already done) is fine; ensure idx[i]/idx[j] indices are read into locals once per swap rather than re-indexed. Minor.
perf.rationale: Reduces redundant array indexing in the partition swap; small constant-factor.
perf.risk: Low impact; only worth it alongside the RangeTree change for consistency. Semantics-preserving.
